title: Give the approximate pKa
asks: A compound is drawn. Write its approximate pKa.

title: Name the mechanism: SN1, SN2, E1 or E2
asks: A reaction and its conditions are given. Say which mechanism operates and which species acts as the base or nucleophile.

title: Circle the stronger nucleophile
asks: Two species are shown. Circle the one that attacks carbon faster.

title: A mechanism from a reagent you know: Grignard and organolithium
asks: A Grignard or organolithium reagent meets a new partner. Draw the mechanism step by step from what you know about the reagent.

title: Circle the faster reaction
asks: Two reactions differ in one thing. Circle the one that goes faster.

title: Two conditions, one product: E2 and E1 mechanisms, and what the NMR says
asks: One substrate gives the same product under two sets of conditions. Draw both mechanisms and interpret a clue from the spectrum.

title: Which statements describe this mechanism? Circle all that apply
asks: Statements about rate law, stereochemistry and solvent are listed. Circle every one that is (or is not) true of the mechanism.

title: Read the energy diagram
asks: Several reaction-coordinate diagrams are drawn. Pick the one that fits the reaction described.

title: Which substrate reacts fastest
asks: Several alkyl halides are listed. Pick the one that reacts fastest (or slowest) by the mechanism named.

title: E2 on a cyclohexane ring: which alkene forms
asks: A substituted cyclohexyl halide meets a strong base. Circle the major elimination product.

title: A chair is drawn: cis or trans, is it the most stable, and if not draw the one that is
asks: A disubstituted cyclohexane is drawn as a chair. Say cis or trans, say whether it is the most stable conformation, and if not draw the most stable one.

title: Analyze the product first: intramolecular SN2 and epoxides
asks: A reactant and an unexpected product are given. Work out which atoms ended up where, then draw the mechanism step by step.

title: Why one ether synthesis works and the other fails
asks: Two ways of joining the same two pieces are tried. One gives the ether, the other does not. Explain with structures and mechanisms.

title: Explain a slow or fast E2 from the chair
asks: One stereoisomer eliminates far more slowly (or faster) than the others. Explain in detail.

title: Pick the efficient route and explain
asks: Two routes to the same product are drawn. Circle the one that gives a clean reaction and explain the choice.

title: Draw the products from their molecular formulas
asks: A reaction gives two products whose molecular formulas are given. Draw each.

title: Substitution or elimination: explain the change in product ratio
asks: The same substrate gives different amounts of substitution and elimination with two different reagents. Explain, naming the reactions.

title: Draw every elimination product
asks: A halide (or dihalide) is treated with base. Draw all the products.

title: Draw both chairs, circle the more stable, name their relationship
asks: A disubstituted cyclohexane is drawn flat with wedges and dashes. Draw both chairs, circle the more stable one, and say whether the two chairs are the same, enantiomers or diastereomers.

title: Carbocation rearrangements and ring expansion
asks: A leaving group departs next to a strained ring or a more substituted carbon. Draw the mechanisms that give the rearranged products.

title: Ring strain: angle strain, torsional strain and the numbers
asks: Compare cycloalkanes: where the strain comes from, how many eclipsing interactions, which ring is most stable and why.

title: Rank acids and bases, and say which factor decides
asks: Several acids (or bases) are given. Put them in order and name the factor that stabilizes the conjugate base.

title: Which way does the equilibrium lie
asks: An acid and a base are mixed. Say which side is favoured, estimate K, or choose a base strong enough to do the job.

title: Make it: from a halide or an alkene to R-H and R-D
asks: A starting material and a product are given. List the steps and reagents.

title: Draw the SN2 product with its stereochemistry
asks: A substrate with a stereocentre meets a good nucleophile. Draw the product, showing inversion.

title: SN1 and E1 products: racemization and the shared carbocation
asks: A substrate ionizes in a polar protic solvent. Draw the substitution and elimination products and their stereochemistry.

title: How the solvent changes the rate
asks: A reaction is run in two solvents. Say which is faster and why, in terms of how the solvent treats the starting materials and the transition state.

title: Saytzeff or Hofmann: which alkene is major
asks: An elimination can give two alkenes. Say which is major and how the leaving group or the base changes the answer.

title: NMR: how many signals, and what a multiplet tells you
asks: A structure is given. Say how many proton or carbon signals it shows, or what a splitting pattern reveals.

title: Draw the transition state
asks: Sketch the transition state of a step, with partial bonds and charges, and compare two transition states.

title: Foundations: the ideas this unit is built on
asks: Quick questions on the general chemistry and early organic chemistry that the unit takes for granted.
